content.title: About
content.content: Abalone is a marine mollusk from the family Haliotidae. It lives in cold coastal waters of the Pacific and Indian Oceans. The flesh is prized for its delicate, slightly sweet flavor and firm yet tender texture. It is commonly used in sushi, salads, pastas, and as a gourmet appetizer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Abalone shells have a pearly interior that is harvested for mother‑of‑pearl jewelry and decorative items.
In Japan it is called “uni‑ko,” and in China “hai‑shou,” and is considered a lucky delicacy.
These mollusks can live up to 30 years and reach lengths over 30 cm.
There are more than 100 species, but Haliotis discus and Haliotis laevigata are most commonly eaten.
Harvesting is regulated in most countries to prevent over‑exploitation.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Abalone provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making it a good source of complete protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafoods, abalone is low in fat, most of which are healthy polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: It contains iron, zinc, magnesium and calcium, supporting blood health, bones and nervous system.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Abalone supplies vitamin B12 and B6, important for metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Shell pigments such as carotenoids have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Mollusks can accumulate cadmium and lead; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Possible parasites
items.content: Raw or undercooked abalone may contain parasites; cook to at least 70 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Abalone is often served lightly seared, baked, or as sashimi. Slice thinly for salads, add to pasta, soups, or prepare in a buttery sauce. Before cooking, remove the shell and rinse the meat under cold water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh abalone in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C, wrapped in a damp cloth, for up to 2 days. Frozen abalone can be stored in an airtight bag for up to 3 months.
